target: Kami tertawa terlalu keras, sampai-sampai tetangga ikut keluar.
english: We laughed too loudly, so much so that the neighbors came out too.
tip: Sampai-sampai = 'so much so that': sampai-sampai dia menangis = to the point that he cried.

target: Anehnya, kunci yang hilang itu muncul lagi di dalam kulkas.
english: Strangely, the lost key turned up again inside the fridge.
tip: Adjective + -nya opens a comment: Anehnya = the strange thing is..., Lucunya = the funny part is...

target: Lucunya, kami berdua membeli kado yang sama untuk orang yang sama.
english: The funny thing is, the two of us bought the same gift for the same person.
tip: Ber- + number = a group of people: kami berdua = the two of us, mereka bertiga = the three of them.

target: Setiap ada tamu, ikan dalam cerita ayah makin lama makin besar.
english: Every time there are guests, the fish in dad's story gets bigger and bigger.
tip: Makin lama makin X = more and more X over time: makin lama makin besar = keeps getting bigger.

target: Ceritakan lagi bagian waktu kamu melompati pagar karena takut anjing kecil itu.
english: Tell again the part when you jumped over the fence because you were afraid of that little dog.
tip: Commands drop meN-: Ceritakan! = Tell it! In statements the full form returns: Dia menceritakan...

target: Apa pun yang terjadi besok, kami tetap berangkat pagi-pagi.
english: Whatever happens tomorrow, we are still leaving early in the morning.
tip: Pun is written separately after question words: apa pun = anything/whatever, siapa pun = anyone.

target: Saya tidak membawa uang tunai satu lembar pun hari ini.
english: I am not carrying even a single bill of cash today.
tip: With a negative, satu + noun + pun = not even one: satu lembar pun = not even one bill.

target: Saya belum pernah terlambat sekali pun selama bekerja di sini.
english: I have never been late even once while working here.
tip: Sekali pun (two words) = even once: belum terlambat sekali pun = never late, not even once.

target: Jangan menyerah, sesulit apa pun soal ujiannya.
english: Don't give up, no matter how difficult the exam questions are.
tip: Se- + adjective + apa pun = no matter how: sesulit apa pun = no matter how difficult.

target: Harga cabai naik terus, bahkan pedagang pun ikut mengeluh.
english: Chili prices keep rising; even the vendors are complaining too.
tip: Bahkan = even, introduces the strongest example: bahkan pedagang pun = even the vendors.

target: Saya cuma mau memastikan jadwal rapat besok tidak berubah.
english: I just want to make sure tomorrow's meeting schedule hasn't changed.
tip: Cuma = only/just, the everyday spoken word; hanya means the same but sounds more careful.

target: Hanya penumpang dengan tiket kelas satu yang boleh masuk ruang tunggu ini.
english: Only passengers with first-class tickets may enter this waiting lounge.
tip: Hanya X yang ... = only X (and no one else): hanya penumpang ini yang boleh masuk.

target: Kamu bisa datang kapan saja, pintu rumah kami selalu terbuka.
english: You can come any time; the door of our house is always open.
tip: Question word + saja = any-: kapan saja = anytime, apa saja = anything, siapa saja = anyone.

target: Adik baru saja tidur, tolong kecilkan suara televisinya.
english: The little one just fell asleep; please turn the TV volume down.
tip: Baru saja = just (moments ago): baru saja tidur = just fell asleep.

target: Anggap saja rumah sendiri, jangan malu-malu.
english: Just treat it like your own home, don't be shy.
tip: Anggap saja = just consider it: anggap saja rumah sendiri = make yourself at home.

target: Perasaan saya saja, atau ruangan ini memang lebih dingin dari biasanya?
english: Is it just my imagination, or is this room really colder than usual?
tip: X saja can mean 'it's just (my) X': perasaan saya saja = it's just my imagination.

target: Setelah tiga kali gagal, akhirnya dia lulus ujian menyetir juga.
english: After failing three times, he finally passed the driving test at last.
tip: Akhirnya ... juga = finally, at last: akhirnya lulus juga = finally passed (after all that).

target: Sudah jam sembilan malam, paket saya belum diantar juga.
english: It's already nine at night and my package still hasn't been delivered.
tip: Belum ... juga = STILL not: belum diantar juga = still hasn't been delivered.

target: Dipikir-pikir, tinggal di kota kecil enak juga.
english: Come to think of it, living in a small town is actually pretty nice.
tip: Juga can soften an opinion: enak juga = actually pretty nice (a mild, pleasant surprise).

target: Dia bukan hanya pintar memasak, tetapi pintar mengatur uang juga.
english: She is not only good at cooking, but good at managing money too.
tip: Bukan hanya X, tetapi Y juga = not only X but also Y.

target: Sejak kuliah di luar kota, dia belajar mengatur uangnya sendiri.
english: Since studying in another city, she has learned to manage her money by herself.
tip: Sendiri after a verb phrase = by oneself: mengatur uangnya sendiri = manage her money herself.

target: Lampu teras itu mati sendiri setiap tengah malam.
english: That porch light turns off by itself every midnight.
tip: Sendiri can mean 'by itself': mati sendiri = went off on its own, nobody touched it.

target: Setiap karyawan bertanggung jawab atas meja kerjanya sendiri.
english: Every employee is responsible for his or her own desk.
tip: Noun + -nya sendiri = one's own: meja kerjanya sendiri = his own desk.

target: Hotelnya bersih, murah, dan dekat pantai pula.
english: The hotel is clean, cheap, and close to the beach as well.
tip: Pula = 'as well/what's more' — a slightly bookish juga: dekat pantai pula = close to the beach too.

target: Memang saya yang salah kemarin, dan saya sudah minta maaf.
english: It really was me who was wrong yesterday, and I have already apologized.
tip: Memang = indeed/admittedly, confirms a fact: memang saya yang salah = it really was my fault.

target: Soal macet, kota ini memang juaranya.
english: When it comes to traffic jams, this city is truly the champion.
tip: Soal X = when it comes to X: soal macet = as for traffic jams.

target: Teman saya bilang, "Filmnya bagus sih, cuma terlalu panjang."
english: My friend said, "The movie's good, I admit — it's just too long."
tip: Sih = spoken particle you'll hear everywhere: bagus sih = it's good, I admit. Recognize it — no need to use it.

target: Motor ini bisa diparkir di mana saja asal tidak menutup jalan.
english: This motorbike can be parked anywhere as long as it doesn't block the road.
tip: Asal = as long as: di mana saja asal tidak menutup jalan = anywhere, provided it doesn't block.

target: Musim kemarau pun, sumur di desa ini tidak pernah kering.
english: Even in the dry season, the well in this village never runs dry.
tip: Noun + pun = even: musim kemarau pun = even (in) the dry season.

target: Tiket konser itu habis dalam lima menit saja.
english: The concert tickets sold out in just five minutes.
tip: Saja comes after the phrase it limits – lima menit saja, not saja lima menit. The reverse of English 'just five minutes'.
